title: Model Alerts

text:
Look at high-confidence mistakes
A confident false positive can reveal a subtraction residual that resembles a PSF. A confident false negative can reveal source crowding, displacement, low contrast or a shape outside the training mixture. Inspect errors by measured SNR and artifact family without discarding inconvenient categories.


Science Explanation

Confidence is not correctness. A score near zero or one may reflect an unfamiliar example being pushed far from the decision boundary. The stratified gallery intentionally overrepresents useful error types; it is not a random sample and must not be used to estimate error rates. Empty error categories are reported honestly instead of filled with another model’s mistakes. Family/SNR tables use the entire eligible evaluation set.


table([dict(population=population, model=model, family=family, **metrics)
       for population, outcomes in reference["breakdowns"].items()
       for model, groups in outcomes.items()
       for family, metrics in groups["family"].items()],
      caption="Complete-evaluation family breakdowns", collapsed=True)
table([dict(population=population, model=model, measured_snr_bin=snr, **metrics)
       for population, outcomes in reference["breakdowns"].items()
       for model, groups in outcomes.items()
       for snr, metrics in groups["snr"].items()],
      caption="Complete-evaluation SNR breakdowns", collapsed=True)
table([dict(population=population, model=model, overlapping_causes=overlap, **metrics)
       for population, outcomes in reference["breakdowns"].items()
       for model, groups in outcomes.items()
       for overlap, metrics in groups["overlap"].items()],
      caption="Coverage of overlapping causes", collapsed=True)
table([dict(population=population, model=model, **r)
       for population, outcomes in reference["high_confidence_mistakes"].items()
       for model, mistakes in outcomes.items() for r in mistakes],
      caption="High-confidence mistakes", collapsed=True)

text:
Try one specified distribution shift
The shift test changes search seeing to σ=1.9\sigma=1.9–2.62.6 pixels and background to 180–300 electrons per pixel, and adds an unseen column-bleed artifact. The reference exposure model and classifier thresholds stay fixed. We report achieved recall, FPR and coverage on these additional fields.
This joint shift changes seeing, background and artifact mixture together. It also increases the mismatch with the fixed 1.4-pixel detection filter, so it cannot identify separate causal contributions or establish general robustness.


Science Explanation

This shift combines broader sources, larger background fluctuations and a new negative family. It can reveal one kind of fragility, but cannot support a claim of general robustness. Changing prevalence alone would not create these image differences. No shifted labels or images choose normalization, architecture, checkpoints, association radius or thresholds. Movers remain a separately identified astrophysical challenge rather than becoming bogus training labels.

An untrailed mover is image-identical to an appearance in one search/reference pair. Its retention is an ontology consistency check; these images do not measure motion. Separate shift-family and overlap tables expose the unseen artifact and association coverage.

section: Reproduce the result, then decide what it supports
text:
Reproduce the result, then decide what it supports
Reference receipts record generator settings, seed blocks, source and artifact hashes, dependencies, hardware descriptions and frozen operating points. Check them before comparing exports. Training data, weights and executed notebooks remain outside Git and outside the standalone HTML. The full reference includes all required investigations; quick smoke exercises APIs and has no scientific performance qualification.


Science Explanation

After provisioning dependencies, execution must work with network access blocked. The public HTML contains the bounded gallery and complete evaluation score/statistic arrays, not the full training set or checkpoints. Its controls need no Bokeh server, Python kernel, WebSocket or API. Source ZIPs, executed notebooks and exported HTML are separate build artifacts. See README and PUBLISHING for commands and the remaining versioned-Pages integration gap. Persistent human annotations, if wanted, use the optional local native review workflow on the newly generated queue. Publication is a later action.

text:
Terminology


PSF


Point-spread function: the pixel distribution of an unresolved source; its integral gives source flux.


reference


An earlier noisy exposure shared by repeated search epochs of one independent field.


search


The newer exposure inspected for positive astrophysical changes.


electron


The detector count unit here; unit gain equates recorded counts and electrons.


flux


Expected total source electrons integrated over the PSF, before finite-image truncation.


background


Expected diffuse electrons per pixel, separate from astronomical source flux.


seeing


Apparent atmospheric source width, modeled here by a Gaussian sigma in pixels.


Poisson


Counting distribution whose variance equals its expected electron count.


read noise


Independent Gaussian detector readout fluctuation with a declared RMS in electrons.


kernel


Fitted convolution weights mapping the reference PSF and photometric scale toward the search exposure.


residual


Search minus its fitted matched-reference-plus-background model.


variance


Expected squared fluctuation in the image unit; variance scales quadratically under unit changes.


covariance


Correlated fluctuations between pixels or observations; omitted from the marginal diagnostic.


SNR


Signal-to-noise ratio; measured detection SNR here is an approximate marginal diagnostic.


candidate


A measured local positive residual maximum passing the frozen detection rule.


association


A truth-only positional rule connecting a measured detection to injected causes.


ambiguous


A detection associated with several genuine changes or a real change overlapping a detector artifact.


field


Independent generated sky/detector scene owning its template, sources, defects and repeated epochs.


epoch


One search observation of a field, with independent search noise.


split


Assignment of independent fields to training, validation or reserved final test roles.


provenance


Recorded origins, identities, labels, seeds and hashes supporting reproducible input relationships.


normalization


Centering/scaling fitted only on training data and applied unchanged to held-out data.


logit


Unbounded classifier output transformed by the sigmoid to a score.


score


Classifier output between zero and one; it need not be a calibrated astrophysical probability.


checkpoint


Saved model parameters selected using development validation loss.


baseline


A simpler measured-data model used to test whether complex learning adds useful information.


permutation


A fixed random reassignment of training labels for a negative-control investigation.


fusion


Combining measured xFit scalar features with image features through native xScan interfaces.


threshold


The inclusive score cutoff used to retain candidates for review.


recall


Retained eligible detected positives divided by all eligible detected positives.


false-positive rate


Retained negatives divided by all eligible negatives, at the specified frozen threshold.


precision


Retained positives divided by all retained candidates; also called purity.


prevalence


Fraction of positives in the candidate population before the classifier threshold.


Brier score


Mean squared difference between a score and its binary label.


reliability


Agreement of average scores with observed positive fractions in occupied score bins.


bootstrap


Resampling independent fields with replacement to quantify specified conditional sampling uncertainty.


distribution shift


A specified change to image or population-generating conditions relative to development.


coverage


The fraction/count of observations for which a stated method or metric is defined and included.


cosmic ray


A modeled compact detector charge event with a morphology distinct from the optical PSF.


misregistration


An offset between reference and search source positions that can create dipolar residuals.


training epoch


One complete pass through the training candidates, distinct from a search-observation epoch.


detection threshold


Minimum positive filtered residual SNR for creating a candidate; distinct from the classifier score threshold.

text:
A.2 Command line
cuphoton --help lists the command groups, one per module:


cuphoton

GPU-accelerated astronomy and imaging tools.

Available groups:
  xdr  xDataReader: GPU-native FITS loading.
  xfit  xFit: Batched nonlinear least-squares fitting for astronomical models.
  ximage  Multi-frame image reconstruction and PSF calibration.
  xpois  Optimal image subtraction for astronomical images.
  xscan  Transient-candidate dataset, training, and review workflows.
  xrep  xRep (xReproject): WCS-aware astronomical image reprojection and stacking.
  xray  GPU-accelerated X-ray detector analysis tools.
  xlens  cuPhoton xLens: scientific monitoring and evidence review.
  xbeam  xBeam: Time-series correlation and VLBI visibility generation.

Use 'cuphoton GROUP --help' for group help.


cuphoton <group> --help lists a group’s commands, and cuphoton <group> help <command> prints one command’s options with their defaults. The command-line index describes every group. Chapter 3 explains the flags that the groups share.
title: Appendix A — Reference

text:
A.3 Python API
Each function’s docstring documents its arguments, defaults and return fields. Print a signature with inspect, or the whole docstring with help:

import inspect
from cuphoton.xrep import reproject_masked_array

print(inspect.signature(reproject_masked_array))

(image: 'np.ndarray', variance: 'np.ndarray', mask: 'np.ndarray', spec: 'ReprojectionSpec', *, backend: 'str | None' = None, prepared: 'PreparedReprojection | None' = None, variance_fill_value: 'float' = nan) -> 'MaskedReprojectionResult'


Each package lists its public names in __all__:

import importlib

print("package          public names")
for name in ("core", "xdr", "xrep", "ximage", "xpois", "xfit", "xscan", "xray", "xbeam", "xlens"):
    package = importlib.import_module(f"cuphoton.{name}")
    print(f"cuphoton.{name:7s} {len(package.__all__):12d}")

xScan and xRay export only their version at the top level. They are command-line tools first. Their reference pages show the submodules to import from, such as cuphoton.xscan.fits_inference and cuphoton.xray.detector_artifacts. Core’s shared code also lives in submodules:

cuphoton.core.fits_io: the FITS reader and its receipts.
cuphoton.core.arrays: helpers that serve NumPy and CuPy arrays with one code path.
cuphoton.core.cli: the command-line framework.
cuphoton.core.executors: Dragon and MPI execution.

text:
A.4 Documents that span modules

Documentation index: entry points to the repository’s guides and references.
Getting started: install profiles and platform notes.
Quickstarts: synthetic smoke runs for xFit, xPois, xScan, xRep and xRay, plus a separate xBeam example.
Command-line index: each group’s commands and the options they share.
Data and artifact contracts: array shapes, axis order, mask rules and the files each run writes.
Architecture: how the modules fit together, and the order auto tries backends in.
Troubleshooting: environment, CUDA, FITS reader and input errors.
Glossary: cuPhoton and astronomy terms.
Changelog: changes and migration notes by release.
title: Appendix A — Reference

text:
A.5 Getting help
cuPhoton has best-effort community support through its GitHub repository. Its support policy gives the details.

Search the GitHub issues for your problem.
If no issue matches, open a bug report with a minimal reproducer. Include the following:

the output of cuphoton --version
the cuPhoton commit, Python version, operating system and installed extras
the command line and the shapes of your inputs
for a GPU problem, the GPU model, driver, CUDA runtime, the backend from summary.json, and whether the CPU profile works

Open a feature request for a new workflow or data contract, or a pull request for a concrete fix.

Remove credentials, private paths and proprietary data from what you post. Do not report security problems on GitHub. Follow the security policy instead.
